encounters.cc: Diffuse bone pain and progressive muscle weakness with chronic diarrhea and 10-pound weight loss

lines: Diffuse bone pain and progressive muscle weakness with chronic diarrhea and 10-pound weight loss
He presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of diffuse bone pain and progressive muscle weakness.
He reports difficulty climbing stairs and getting up from a seated position.
He also mentions experiencing chronic diarrhea, bloating, and a weight loss of 10 pounds over the last year.
He denies any history of fractures or trauma.
- Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection with history of AIDS-defining illnesses
- Peripheral sensory neuropathy secondary to chronic arsenic toxicity
- Bictegravir/Tenofovir alafenamide/Emtricitabine 1 tablet oral daily (intermittent adherence due to social circumstances)
- Sulfamethoxazole/Trimethoprim 1 double-strength tablet oral daily for PCP prophylaxis
Occupation: Construction laborer and seasonal agricultural pesticide applicator.
Physical examination reveals mild pallor and diffuse tenderness over the long bones.
Neurological examination shows proximal muscle weakness without sensory deficits.
A dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) scan shows a T-score of -2.5 at the lumbar spine.

lines: Fatigue, weight loss, night sweats, and sensation of fullness in the left upper quadrant
Patient with HIV returns for hematology follow-up three months after gastroenterology evaluation.
He presents with three-month history of fatigue, weight loss, and night sweats.
He also reports feeling of fullness in left upper quadrant.
- Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection with history of AIDS-defining illnesses

Occupation: Construction laborer and seasonal agricultural pesticide applicator.
On physical examination, he appears pale and has splenomegaly.
His complete blood count shows a white blood cell count of 150,000/µL, hemoglobin of 10 g/dL, and platelet count of 450,000/µL.
Differential count reveals 6% myeloblasts, 4% promyelocytes, 40% myelocytes, 20% metamyelocytes, 10% bands, and 20% segmented neutrophils.
A bone marrow biopsy is performed, and cytogenetic analysis demonstrates the presence of the Philadelphia chromosome.

lines: Fatigue, abdominal discomfort, intermittent diarrhea, and progressive burning pain with numbness in feet

Over the past week, he has developed numbness and tingling in both feet, which is now accompanied by burning pain in his calves.

He works as a pesticide sprayer for a commercial farm and admits he often skips wearing gloves.
He denies alcohol use or recent travel.
Physical examination shows hyperpigmented skin with scattered areas of hypopigmentation on the trunk and neck.
Neurologic testing reveals symmetric stocking–glove sensory loss and decreased ankle reflexes bilaterally.
Laboratory testing shows mild anemia and slightly elevated liver enzymes.

lines: Persistent diarrhea, abdominal pain, and 10-pound weight loss with occasional night sweats

lines: Three-week history of cough, low-grade fever, night sweats, and 10-pound weight loss

He presents with a three-week history of cough, low-grade fever, night sweats, and reports a 10-pound weight loss during this period.

The patient works in construction and recently participated in a project near the Mississippi River.
He denies any recent travel outside of the United States.
On physical examination, the patient appears fatigued.
Auscultation of the lungs reveals crackles at the right lung base.
Skin examination shows a few verrucous skin lesions on his arms.
Sputum culture grows broad-based budding yeast.
Chest X-ray: Right lower lobe infiltrate

lines: Three-day history of fever, productive cough with yellowish sputum, and pleuritic chest pain

The patient is a 46-year-old male with HIV infection with history of AIDS-defining illnesses, chronic myeloid leukemia on imatinib therapy, and recent pulmonary blastomycosis, who presents with a three-day history of fever, productive cough with yellowish sputum, and pleuritic chest pain.
He reports no recent travel or sick contacts.

His temperature is 38.9°C (102°F), blood pressure is 120/75 mmHg, pulse is 110 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute.
Physical examination reveals dullness to percussion and increased tactile fremitus over the right lower lung field.
Breath sounds are diminished in this area with egophony.
His CD4 count is 350 cells/mm³ and his HIV viral load is undetectable.

lines: Night sweats, fever, 10-pound weight loss, fatigue, and swelling in neck and groin with acute neurological changes
This 47-year-old male with HIV infection, prior AIDS-defining illnesses, and chronic myeloid leukemia presents with a 2-month history of night sweats, fever, and a 10-pound weight loss.
He reports feeling fatigued and has noticed swelling in his neck and groin.
His CD4 count six months ago was 250 cells/mm³.
